Personality

Sousborg is a very serious chef, who asks Clover what to do when fighting him. He speaks with a clear french accent and is happy when Clover gives him the right instructions on how to cook an egg.

Main Story
Pacifist Route

Sousborg does not appear in the pacifist route due to the kitchen being blocked off.

Neutral and Genocide Route

Sousborg is a scripted encounter. He attacks Clover in the kitchen area of the Factory.

In Battle
Attacks

Strategy

When Clover goes to the ACT menu, Sousborg will challenge them to tell them how to prepare an egg. The order of the correct ACTs are Crack, Fry, and Season.

Quotes

entries.name: Guardener.
entries.content:
Guardener is the miniboss of the Steamworks, encountered in the Greenhouse.

The Guardener is a tall robot with large pistons for arms, red eyes, a Royal Guard Sign on her torso, and a thick cylinder on her head that gives the appearance of a hat. She is evidently quite old due to the obvious damage (in particular her missing legs, which appear to have been torn off), coupled with the overgrown flora on top of her head.

Personality

The Guardener is a defense-robot first, protecting the Steamworks' garden as if it were her own kin. Upon finding one of the flowers squished, she first labels Clover as a level-3 threat, before quickly escalating the situation to a level-10 and attempting to execute them immediately. The Guardener isn't very social either, as when the backup robots asked to be called "just to hang out," they were met with silence.

However, that isn't to say that the Guardener isn't a complete murder-happy nature machine, as shown when 3 had arrived late and gave it a flower as a consolation prize, allowing it to still attack even when it had showed up late. She is also shown to be polite, being very calm with Clover and Ceroba before accidentally labeling them as a level-10 threat due to a malfunction. Though after the battle, she could not understand why her creator, the head office or anyone else at Steamworks was unavailable for her report, and regretted ever waking up.

Main Story
Neutral/Pacifist Route

Guardener ambushes Clover and Ceroba Ketsukane when they are leaving the Greenhouse. Because they trampled on the white flowers on the path before her, she tries to report them to staff for a level 3 offense, but malfunctions and accidentally reports it as a "LEVEL 10 THREAT" which is punished by extermination. If Clover defeats her by fighting, as she dies, she states that while Clover may not care about the flowers, but to her, "the garden" is beautiful. If Clover defeats her by correcting her malfunction, Guardener realizes the current state of the area and tries and fails to correctly report the offense as a level 3 and contact her creator (of unknown identity) before noticing her surroundings. Realizing her "day has passed", she leaves Clover alone and chooses to hibernate, stating that "life was better not knowing".

During the Neutral ending fight, she is summoned to serve as an attack.

At the end of the True Pacifist ending, she is still shown hibernating as one of her Backups is seen holding a flower before leaving with another robot.

Genocide Route

When Clover gets to Guardener, she can be seen being told by Axis to stay put in order to be safe from them. When she sees them, she quickly goes back into the ground. Thus, her fight gets skipped.

In Battle
During Guardener's battle, she will ensnare Clover in white vines, incapacitating the FIGHT, ACT, ITEM, and MERCY buttons. They can be released by pressing each of them three times, which will waste a turn each time.

Attacks

A piston arm descends from the top of the left side of the box. A piston arm descends from the top of the right side of the box, only extending halfway down before retracting, and a piston arm ascends from the bottom of the right side of the box that extends halfway up before retracting.
A single piston will be released horizontally, followed by 4 plants that shoot a pellet upwards.
A single plant will bud followed by three pistons extending leftward that progressively get lower from the top of the bullet box. None of these pistons touch the flower.
A gear in a random corner will repeatedly shoot pellets in eight directions at a consistent interval.
A gear slides into the middle of the bullet box and spews continuous lasers while spinning in one direction. At a point in time, it reverses its direction.
A gear slides from the bottom before a piston crushes it, making the gear explode into large fragments.
A gear slides in a horizontal direction into its respective corner. A piston then extends vertically from the opposite vertical side to crush the gear into seven bits that will rise up before falling. Bits will arc toward the opposite side horizontally.
Plants will grow from every side, each one shooting one pellet, in counterclockwise order starting from the left part of the bottom side. Each side fits three plants.
Two mini-robots will be summoned. The one on the right (hereby referred to as Righty) will go to the SOUL's vertical position and shoot its pistol, firing a bullet horizontally. The one on the left (hereby referred to as Lefty) will go to that same vertical position with a slight delay and hold out a shield, which breaks the bullet and splits it into three fragments going right at either a 45 degree angle either way or without an angle. Each fragment has a different angle. This cycle repeats four times.
The robots will throw an assortment of items like axes, swords, and cement bricks.
Two pistons from the top-right and bottom-left will extend vertically, extending halfway across the box before stopping. Lefty will fire a bow and arrow toward the SOUL with projectiles affected by gravity. If on the right, Righty will fire its pistol in the same manner as the previous gun attack, but the bullet shatters when it hits the piston. Lefty will fire four times before the attack ends.
A third robot will appear after the other two robots have left. It will appear on the left-side of the bullet box with a gun. It will aim at the SOUL with a red line indicating the shot, and will stop aiming a moment before shooting. It shoots 11 times.
The two robots will return and throw grenades and dynamite which will explode a moment after entering the bullet box.
Strategy

Clover needs to release all 4 buttons to be able to use the 3 other ACTs. Clover is then able to spare Guardener by Pleading 5 times to fully lower their offense level. Going for the ITEM button first allows Clover to use healing items, as no other buttons can provide high HP restoration.

The attack pattern will not change, so remember which turn you are on and look at the attacks in preparation. However, on the 9th turn, the attack will randomize until all menus have been clipped. Only then will the pattern continue.

On the turn that you get all menus free, the two-piston attack with Lefty and Right will start. It is highly recommended to choose the top-left, as Righty can't shoot if you're behind an arm. However, if you choose the bottom-right, not only can Lefty hit you, but Righty can shoot his bullets which WILL shatter and you will need to dodge the fragments alongside the arrows.

entries.name: Dina.
entries.content:
Dina is a vendor in the Wild East. Being the bartender in the saloon, she sells a variety of consumables.

This Town]
Oh this little place? It's pretty fun 'round here. I heard it was established some years back when the Dunes gained its name if you get me.
I should be polished on its history but Star don't talk 'bout those days.
I was lookin' for a friendly environment to share my brewin' skills, so here I am.
There ain't terribly much to do in this town but that only makes it more close-knit.
Every day has been pretty predictable until you showed up. I'm eager to see what Star's plannin'.
[Your snakes]
Haha, I get this question a lot.
These fellas are my pets. Real reptiles, not monsters.
Their names are Ann, Sammy, and Bert.
The Underground still houses some critters from the Surface like birds and insects.
I found these west of here, hidin' in a crevasse of sorts.
Some monsters think keepin' pets is strange but I think it's cute.
They give me someone to talk to when business is slow.
[Can I leave?]
You can at any time. Won't hurt my feelin's.
Oh... I see. Star's tryin' to keep you here since it's a big deal and all.
That ain't right if you're wantin' to go.
I try not to infringe on sheriff business but I'll ask him 'bout it soon.
I'm sure he means well by it!
[North Star]
What a character! Our big and courageous sheriff.
I get a feelin' he ain't as tough as he likes to play up.
But then again, maybe he's just clumsy. His whole posse is a hoot.
They frequently host parties here.
He definitely knows the right kind of monsters to surround himself with.
Not to mention Ceroba, his childhood friend.
I get a kick out of her and Star's antics.
When she brings her daughter into town, it's basically two against one, haha!
Now that I think about it, it's been a while since I saw the rascal.
We really need to get the whole gang together again!
[Trying to Talk after the Feisty Four leave Starlo]
It’s probably not the best time to chat. Real worried ‘bout everythin’ goin’ on right now.
[Feisty Five]
Was all the drama settled? It was real rough out there.
The Five are like siblin's, ya know? Every now and then a spat rears its head.
'Course, most of the time it's somethin' like Mooch stealing Ed's hat or Star forgettin' to turn off his "mission machines" out in the Dunes.
This was uh... This was a step above.
It ain't my business but I'm sure it'll all smooth over in time... 'least I hope.
Family, right?
[Kanako]
Ceroba's little troublemaker. Real cute kid.
She likes to hand 'round us and the Five when her mom's in town.
Looks dang intimidatin' in a cowboy hat too, that's for sure. Little older and she would fit right into our group!
Though I don't think Ceroba would allow it seein' as we might not be the best influence, haha.
Anyway, I been meanin' to ask Ceroba where Kanako's been. School field trip maybe? She does like to travel 'round the Underground.
Though I wouldn't think she'd be allowed too far ever since...
Ah, well, I could tell stories for hours but that's the gist of it, heh...
[Government]
Heard fears of Royal's bargin' into town? Your presence did cause a stir. Only natural.
The government takes human business seriously. Very seriously...
I'm sure you've been hunted and attacked a hundred times by now. Happens every once in a while when a human falls down here.
Man, if I didn't have a business to upkeep I'd let whoever's wronged you have it!
[Government (NEW)]
Hey, if you're worried the town's gonna be ransacked, I wouldn't be.
Royal's don't come 'round here often. I don't think they much care what we do.
To my knowledge, last time any representative showed up was to post a flier on the news board. A notice for some kinda new healthcare program.
Ol' Fluffybuns and his posse aren't exactly the most active group.
Other than chasin' the odd human, I don't think they have anything else to spend their time on.
It seems monsterkind has peaked in a way, so I reckon everyone should just come out here and spend their G on a slice of the Surface! Haha.
[Chujin]
Oh, Ceroba's partner? Um, well, kind of a heavy subject...
He never really came 'round this town back in the day. Didn't like what it stood for. Not that the tension was one-sided.
Whether it was politics or an unburied hatchet, Star didn't speak highly of the fella neither.
There was one time though...
It was after hours - no one here but me. BAM! Front doors swing open and in walks Chujin.
He was breathin' heavy, worn n' rugged... Unusual for a cleancut monster of science.
I didn't think he drank but nevertheless, he sat down and ordered a cold one.
I asked if somethin' was the matter but all he said was, "I believe I've seen a ghost."
Weird, huh? Like... a monster? Couldn't be what he meant, right? Who knows...
Shoot, I've said too much haven't I?
All in all, I wouldn't bring him up 'round Star or Ceroba. There's a lotta feelin's there, ya know...
[Chujin (NEW)]
Sorry but I need to be more careful of what beans I spill.
It ain't becomin' to spread gossip while a widow's still in mourning.
Exit

Have fun out there! [Upon exiting]
Genocide Route

...I ain't gonna make you a drink if that's what you want.

I know what you did...Naive fool...I tried to warn him. And Ceroba...She lost to you? You must be feelin' real lucky. ... I have nothin' but hatred runnin' through me, but I know I wouldn't stand a chance. So here I am, cooped up while everyone else... If you aren't going to kill me, let me mourn my family in peace. Star might've only been a target to you but... He was more of a hero than you'll ever be. Now... Get out of my Saloon.

entries.name: Blackjack.
entries.content:
Blackjack is a vendor in the Wild East who sells weapons and armor.


Blackjack has the following items for sale:

Gunpowder for 40 G
Silver Ammo for 80 G
Fancy Holster for 50 G
Wild Revolver for 200 G (Clover cannot buy it, as they are a child, but later obtains it from Starlo)
Profile
Appearance

Blackjack is a man with bright purple skin with a large, gray handlebar mustache, wearing a desaturated dark blue hat and wearing round glasses. As for clothes, he wears a black vest, a dark purple bowtie, desaturated dark blue pants, and a black shoe. He seems to be obese and is missing his right leg, which is replaced by a wooden one.

Personality

Blackjack is your typical western blacksmith, selling items like Gunpowder and a Wild Revolver, although the latter is later given to Clover by Starlo. He's upbeat and slightly eccentric, willing to sell anything to and take anything off Clover's hands. Notably, he despises the Feisty Four, calling them "five demonic youngsters," before immediately calling other residents delightful.

He can be extremely reckless sometimes, as when Clover asks Blackjack about his wares, he flashes his revolver to Clover, then states that he has better aim with his revolvers than North Star (Starlo). Afterwards, he begins spinning his revolver, causing it to discharge in the opposite direction which startles him, dropping the gun.

He can also come off morally ambiguous, as when Clover asks about visitors, Blackjack flashes a revolver to Clover, while stating that he's not a fan of violence himself, and then asks them to not further question his morality. Furthermore, he states that he makes sure that his wares aren't lethal, but they could be since even everyday items like Ballet Shoes could be lethal as well.

He's also a hypocrite. In his shop dialogue, he mentions he isn't "selling ultra-deadly weapons with anyone with enough G." However, despite at first not wanting to sell his revolvers to Clover, he later sells the gun to Starlo for 400G without question.

Main Story
Neutral Route

Pacifist Route

Blackjack can be encountered when first entering the Town. During Mission 2, Starlo goes to Blackjack's Shop to sell the Wild Revolver to Clover, Which fails, and then Starlo offers 400G to Blackjack before Clover obtains the Wild Revolver.

Genocide Route

Like most vendors, Blackjack is absent in the Genocide route. You also cannot steal any gold from him, as he’s likely taken it from his safe and brought it with him when he evacuated. The Wild Revolver is also obtained before heading into the town square, so it’s unavailable to be purchased in the shop.

Dialogue
Before buying something

Greetings! Take a gander. Just don't touch anything. [Upon entrance]
Change your mind? [Upon exiting a menu]
Buy

Interested in anything? [While purchasing]
I thank you! [On purchase]
I need the proper sum... [If not enough G]
You have your hands full. [If inventory is full]
Sell

Thank you! I will make good use of this.
Talk

Ask away!
[The Feisty Five]
I was hoping you wouldn’t ask about them…
Sigh…
Young hooligans are all they are.
Hooligans I’m forced to put with to keep my business afloat.
They have no respect for the fine arms I produce, always waving them around like they’re some child’s toy!
However, I have learned how to benefit off their behavior.
I’m the only monster around here that provides such quality weapons, so whenever they push me, I push back and threaten to close shop.
They always crumble and end up paying far more than the weapon they want is worth.
A little money is worth a few headaches, haha!
[Your Wares]
Ah yes, my gallery of babies!
Uh… That sounded strange… Ahem!
These beauties are all crafted from the highest quality materials!
I forge them myself in my personal gunsmithing room!
Not only do I make them with care, but I also care FOR them.
I start my mornings by polishing the whole stock until I see my reflection in them!
I also know how to handle these bad boys. I’m a way better shot than North Star, that’s for sure.
(Blackjack's gun goes off)
I… I saw a bandit in my rafters.
[Visitors]
The Wild East gets many visitors each day.
There’s something about the aura here that some monsters can’t get enough of.
Now, don’t worry. I’m not selling ultra-deadly weapons to any passerby with enough G.
I make sure my wares are tame enough to not be lethal. I myself am not one for violence!
Well… used enough times consecutively, they COULD be lethal. But then again, a ballet shoe could also be lethal used enough times.
Look, don’t question my morality too much! I am not prepared to speak about it!
[History]
I heard about this town some years back.
I had mastered my smithing capabilities and was looking to open up shop.
As it turns out, there was an empty building here so I thought “why not?” Seemed like quite the perfect town for such a shop.
Do I regret settling down here, resulting in endless torment from five demonic youngsters? Every day.
But everyone else I’ve met is quite pleasant, so it balances out.
[Trying to Talk after the Feisty Four leave Starlo]
What occurred in the square?
North Star just walked by my shop while staring at the ground.
It isn’t a trouble of mine but… maybe you should check in on him?
If you think it’s important that is. Ahem.
[Your Age]
How old am I? How old do I look?
Believe it or not, I was born with gray hair. Got it from my father.
But yes... I am what they call a "senior citizen." Which only means I am much wiser than you youngsters!
Because I've been around, I do have some interesting history if you would like to hear it.
[Your History (NEW)]
I was born during the war. Mere weeks before our Underground imprisonment.
My father was a soldier in King ASGORE's army. And a soldier was all he ever became.
When my mother got the word that monsterkind had to withdraw, she refused to leave. Insisted on searching for my father instead.
...Despite pleas from officers, there was no changing her mind.
I was promptly given to a nanny and raised in this very mountain.
But so goes life in such circumstances. Not everyone gets it easy.
I will say, these kids out here... While they can be bothersome, they are lucky.
The Underground isn't ideal but from the ripples I grew up feeling, it is much better than the strife of days past.
I'm thankful for that.
[The Four]
North Star's posse are friends of his from highschool, I believe.
There, they started a club to talk about movies and dress up and go on imaginary adventures. Almost like a permanent Pumpkin Day.
Some think that they're a little old to be doing such things but it's pretty harmless.
...What am I saying? It isn't harmless! They harm me almost every day!
Did you know that Ace and Mooch installed a speaker system throughout the town?
They use it to play little jingles and this dreadful song that loops over and over! It even changes arrangements in certain buildings!
Every morning at seven they wake me up with an eagle screech!
I've tried telling Ace that it's SUPPOSED to be a rooster crow but he always says "Roosters and crows can't get together like that."
They COULD if it was true LOVE!!!
(Pant... pant...)
...
...What were we speaking about?
[Humans]
Humans, huh?
Well, I'm afraid there's no sugar-coating it. Humans such as yourself are widely disdained in the Underground.
It's popular to root for their annihilation, even.
So much loss... So much grief...
The wicked actions of humankind are forever etched in our history, only to subside once King ASGORE obtains seven of their SOULs and judgment is brought upon the Surface.
Then you wonder, "How can a town like the Wild East exist in such a society?" Well it isn't without its controversy.
Most are indifferent, preferring not to acknowledge it.
But some make their opinions very clear, stating that the town's making light of a serious situation, or even that we're traitors to monsterkind itself.
Rather harsh, right?
I believe everyone who participates is just fascinated with the Surface world. Whether it be historical, or plain old escapism.
There's nothing wrong with finding an appreciation for such things, the way I see it.
[Your Opinion (NEW)]
My opinion on humans? Hmm...
I've spent most of my life disliking humans outright. Justifiably so.
But... as I've aged, I've pondered over my bitterness.
Thought that perhaps, this feud is more nuanced than it first appears?
But even with all my years, I still haven't reached the other side, if I ever will.
I do know that I dislike the nature that drove humankind to do what they did.
The violence, the selfishness...
But that nature can reside in anyone.
At the end of the day, it's about an individual's character, you see.
Whether or not they carry civility and respect within their SOUL.
So far, I see those traits in you, so I've given you a pass.
And anyway, it would be foolish of me to eliminate a potential patron when they have money to spend, haha!
[Smithing]
My life's dedication!
I work with steel, iron, and even a little silver and gold when I'm feeling fancy.
Mining Co. is still uncovering many such materials so I buy it from them at the beginning of each month.
Creating practical and beautiful items from rubble is endearing. I learned everything I know from a job in New Home where I made armor for Royal Guards.
The head smith who taught me - rumor was that he helped King ASGORE forge his mighty trident.
Of course, naysayers tout that it's made of pure magic but I don't believe them!
You do know that ASGORE wields a trident, correct? An absolute masterwork it is!
His armor is wonderfully crafted as well. I've heard it's impenetrable!
Such a respectable monster must look the part and he spared no expense!
Exit

I wish you good travels! [Upon exiting]

entries.name: Flower girls.
entries.content:
The Flower girls are encountered in the dunes.

The Flower Girls are humanoid monsters who have an appearance similar to southern belles, wearing long dresses, wide brimmed hats, and gloves. They each only have one eye visible at all times, with the other being covered by their hats (and in the case of Violetta, her hair). The flowers they hold and the color of their clothes correspond with the flowers they are named after (with the exception of Pedla, who isn't named after a specific flower).

Personality

Each Flower Girl has a distinct personality, though they all share a love for flowers.

Violetta

Violetta is shy and awkward. During her battle, she is shown to be somewhat self loathing, agreeing with Clover if they choose to insult her, and believing she deserves her injury when damaged.

Pedla

Pedla is friendly and outgoing. She kindly offers Clover flowers throughout her battle, regardless of their actions.

Rosa

Rosa is prideful and obnoxious. Throughout her battle, she boasts about her flowers and acts sassy towards Clover. When talked to in the overworld, she reveals that she finds her sisters annoying.

All Routes

One Flower Girl is randomly selected to appear as a scripted encounter in the room before Clover meets up with Martlet for a second time. The room contains three different flowers on a small patch of grass, each representing one of the Flower Girls.

Pacifist Route

Like other Dunes enemies, the Flower Girls can be found as overworld NPCs once the player completes the Dunes during the Pacifist Route. Violetta is found inside of the structure housing the sprout in Oasis Valley, Pedla is found in the room where the player encounters one of the Flower Girls as an enemy, and Rosa is found in the room after where El Bailador is fought. They also appear in the credits of the Pacifist ending. Violetta is shown tending to the Oasis Valley sprout, and Pedla and Rosa are shown selling Flowers in the Wild East.

Attacks

Growing Flowers: Large droplets of water appear from the top of the bullet board. Upon hitting the bottom, a tall vine grows and three droplets appear from the droplet.
Colored Flowers: Flowers quickly move from left to right or vice versa. The petals on these flowers can be colored either blue or orange.
Spinning Flowers: A giant flower petal rotates either clockwise or counter-clockwise.
Falling Flowers: Flowers are tossed from either side of the bullet alongside a green flower. This attack happens after selecting Encourage (Violetta), Accept (Pedla) or Inquire (Rosa).
Strategy

In order to defeat the Flower Girls, you must Encourage Violetta, Accept Pedla's flower, and Inquire for Rosa, then catch the green flower that appears when they begin throwing flowers.

Quotes

D-Don't mind me. [Neutral]

I can do this... [Neutral]

I know... sorry... [Insult]

Pedla

Would you like any flowers my dear? [Neutral]

Here you go! [Accept]
Here... [Accept, Low HP]
Do you really mean that, hun? Gosh, you've made me the happiest florist around town! [Flatter]
Gosh, hun. What are you on about? [Flatter, Low HP]
Oh, come now, deary. I bet my flowers would look very pretty on your hat! [Deny]
About what I expected... [Deny, Low HP]
It's never too late to accept a sign of friendship, you know. [Low HP]
I...I'm okay. [Low HP]
Rosa

Flowers make a monster stronger! [Neutral]
If you want a flower from me, you gotta prove yourself! [Neutral]
Flowers are great! Orange, blue, yellow... gotta love 'em! [Neutral]
My flowers are top of the line! [Neutral]
Pah! Don't I know it! [Flatter]
Better than yours. [Flatter, Low HP]
I don't know, CAN YOU? [Inquire]
Ooo, edgy. [Inquire, Low HP]
SORRY ABOUT THAT!!! Haha. [Insult]
Come on, where'd you learn to insult? [Insult, Low HP]
You're kind of a jerk, you know that? [Low HP]
Just gotta hold on. [Low HP]
Trivia
The Flower Girls were the winning entry of an enemy design contest held by the Undertale Yellow development team. They were designed by AeroArtwork, who would eventually join the game's development team in its later years of development.
Despite being a scripted encounter, they will not appear if the Dunes’ kill counter is already depleted.
Rosa is one of the monsters present on the list of people Chuijin has befriended found in the Ketsukane House.
A flower girl is a young female who scatters flower petals down the aisle during a wedding procession.

entries.name: Bowll.
entries.content:
Bowll is a monster encountered in the dunes.

Appearance

Bowll is a bull with a bowl for a body. Cracks appear all over its body, with its tail notably having a spinning plate on the end. Occasionally during battle, the annoying dog may pop up out of the bowl for a few second, before going back into the bowl.

After cleaning him, he noticeably sparkles.

Personality

Bowll is notably furious and lashes out at Clover at the start of the battle, being insecure about the state of his body. After being consoled, he's less prone to fighting and is willing to discover his true self.

Attacks

Bull: Bulls appear around the bullet board, and parallel to them appear red cloths. When a red cloth appears, a bull runs towards it, damaging the SOUL if run into.
Liquid: The bullet board shifts into a halfway-full mug. Marshmallows are repeatedly tossed from the top which makes the liquid rise until it is almost full.
Silverware: Two sets of silverware fill the bullet board, with one half descending and the other ascending.
Test Song: Unused in final game. identical to El Bailador's attacks. likely used to test how El Bailador would work as bowll is very close to them in the files
Strategy

In order to spare Bowll, you must Console him once, telling him he's fine the way he is. Afterwards, you must clean, after which you can spare him.

Flavor Text

Quotes

Take it easy, pal! [Clean, Low HP]

Y-You watch your mouth! [Taunt]
What's so funny, huh? [Taunt, Low HP]
But I... I am tough. [Console]
Really? You mean it? [Console #2]
You're the one that should be careful! [Console, Low HP]

It'll t-take more than that to take me down! [Low HP]
Trivia
Bowll Annoying Dog
The Annoying Dog popping out of Bowll's back
Bowll is a combination of the words "bowl" and bull" [?]
Bowll, appearing to be made out of porcelain, may be a pun on the phrase "bull in a China shop", which is used to describe someone who is reckless in situations that require carefulness.
Sometimes, the Annoying Dog will pop out of Bowll's back and wink at the player.

entries.name: Cactony.
entries.content:
Cactony is a monster encountered in the dunes.

Appearance

Cactony appears to be a regular cactus with 2 arms. Its body/stem is slightly curved with multiple spines pointing out, mostly seen on the side. It also has a face, composing of 2 blank eyes and a mouth. Depending on its battle status, it makes different facial expressions.

Personality

Cactony desires love and affection, but is well aware of what it is.

Attacks

Needle Top: A sphere appears at the top of the Battle Box and shoots several projectiles towards the SOUL's location. After landing, it stays for a second before disappearing.
Needle Side: Needles will be shot from either side of the Bullet Box and then arc downwards. After landing, it stays for a second before disappearing. When the Touch ACT is used, some needles get green areas between them which provide healing and make Cactony spareable.
Strategy

Cactony can be spared by selecting the Touch ACT. This prompts a regular Needle Side attack with green areas between some needles, which need to be entered to make Cactony spareable.

Flavor Text

Cactony comes to share his pain. [Encounter]
Lacks physical affection. [Check]

entries.name: Sir Slither.
entries.content:
Sir Slither is a monster encountered in the dunes

Sir Slither is a monster resembling a red snake with a yellow underbelly and a brown hood. It sits in a purple vase with yellow handles and a stripe pattern.

Attacks

Pottery: A warning appears as pottery forms in the middle of the Bullet Box. Several bullets fly through the box before two snakes rise up and shape a pot.
Snake: Snakes slither vertically or horizontally through the Bullet Box.
Strategy

In order to spare Sir Slither, you must go to act, doubt them twice in a row, and then you can spare Sir Slither. If you choose to believe Sir Slither, a thick fog will emerge and partially obscure the screen. This effect ends once the turn has ended.

entries.name: Dunebud.
entries.content:
Dunebud is a monster encountered in the dunes.

Dunebud is seemingly a sort of slime monster, made of sand with what appears to be a patch of dirt on their head. The patch of dirt also has a sapling sprouting from it.

Personality

Dunebud is a monster of few words, but they're presented as very playful and eager to have fun.

Appears With

Another Dunebud
Attacks

Sandcastle: Places a bucket in the Bullet Box and builds a sandcastle. The sandcastle shoots arrows towards the SOUL.
Tumbleweeds: A series of tumbleweeds move in the Bullet Box horizontally from one side to the other.
Chase: Enters the Battle Box and leaps at the SOUL vertically whenever it is above or below them. This continues a few times. If it is at low HP, then it does not jump when using this attack and moves slower.
Strategy

To spare Dunebud, you must select the ACT button, and either Shoo Dunebud twice, or select Jiggle and then Pat. During the sandcastle attack, moving slowly will help you survive, and during the leap attack, moving fast will help.

Flavor Text

Looking for some fun. [Check]
Dunebud popped out of the sand. [Encounter]
Double trouble! [Encounter with a second Dunebud]
Dunebud is getting antsy. [Neutral]

entries.name: The Feisty four (Or the Feisty five)
entries.content:
The Feisty Four are a set of minibosses encountered in the Wild East. Alongside their leader, North Star, they form the Feisty Five (Fearlessness, Excellence, Intuition, Sneakiness, Toughness, Youthfulness, and Justice. The J is silent.), a gang who rules the town. Gang members, aside from North Star, are Ed, Moray, Ace and Mooch.

Starlo (boss)
Gillbert (Moray's father)
Angie (Moray’s mother)

Appearance

Ed is a large, pink ogre-like monster. He has a circular body and wears a fancy tuxedo-esque outfit, with the shirt being sleeveless. His face has large bushy eyebrows, as well as a single square tooth sticking out his mouth upwards.

Moray is a blue, humanoid monster with fish elements. They wear a beret and musketeer-like armor. Additionally, their eyes are covered up by their hair, which itself appears to sweep to the side.

Ace is a grey humanoid monster, donning a fancy tuxedo and a top hat. His facial features are obscured by a shadow being casted from his top hat that covers a majority of his face, with the exception of his left eye.

Mooch is a grey squirrel monster with purple hair. She wears a large green hat with holes for her ears to pop out of, as well as a green jacket with a purple shirt. She also wears no shoes and has 3 toes. Additionally, she wears a green scarf that slightly obscures her mouth.

Personality

Ed is a fearless and tough monster. He is also the most temperamental character in the posse, but he recognizes it and states that he wants to work on it. In addition, he wants to learn how to play the guitar, but due to him being bigger than the others, he can not play it. Ed is the first one to speak up for the group and tries to deliver justice when Starlo leaves the Feisty Four and Clover alone. Furthermore, he is optimistic and apologizes for his actions, as he tells Clover he is sorry for being so forceful earlier when they arrived at the Wild East.

Moray represents the E and Y in Feisty, being Excellence and Youthfulness respectively. They are the only member of the four (without counting their boss) that is known to keep contact with their parents. Moray is also more caring and sympathetic towards Martlet, as they bring her food even though it is not mealtime. They are also the one that stays more in-character when the posse are acting for a mission for Clover in comparison to some of the other members. When the group wishes Clover and Martlet good luck on the Pacifist Route, Moray is the last to leave, giving the pair one last look before departing, showing that they really got attached to the two. In addition, they have a passion for music, as in the neutral route they are seen playing the guitar on the saloon.

Ace is the most serious member of the posse. Due to this, he is seen reacting to the other three shenanigans with face palms at the end of the true pacifist route. But this does not mean that he joins as well at some of the adventures of the Feisty Four. As Blackjack states that he and Mooch installed the speaker system throughout the town, using it to play an eagle screech and play jingles and songs. Ace is also the one that represents the I in feisty, this letter representing intuition. He also describes himself as “2D as my cards” but doesn’t seem to be bothered by that. Moreover, he notices smaller details, like for example, when Clover’s hat was practically decomposing before the duel.

Mooch is the only one in the group that commits crimes, this being pickpocketing and thievery. She is sneaky and is the representative of the S in Feisty, which stands for Sneakiness. As Ace stated, she is the only one that never oversteps her boundaries. She likes shiny items, as she remarks that the gun that North Star gave to Clover is awfully shiny. Mooch sometimes makes sarcastic remarks, since she tells Ace to not be so kind when he doesn’t even ask for her help in the Feisty Four battle. Despite this, Mooch can be kind when she wants to be. If Clover kills Starlo and returns to the Wild East, Mooch is seen in front of the Five's house and apologizes on behalf of the group if she is talked to. It is also implied in the neutral route that Mooch is the youngest member of the posse, since Dina doesn’t let her sneak a drink.

Main Story
Neutral Route

The Neutral Route is rather similar to that of the Pacifist.

Pacifist Route

They first appear before Clover and Martlet when they approach the town, with Moray being the first and altering the others. Ed gives a dark joke about them killing the last person that came to town before being told off by Moray. Ace then reprimands the two of them for being so threatening before Martlet and Clover prepare to leave. North Star then arrives and apologizes for how his "posse" treated them before explaining themselves as "The Feisty Five". North Star then realizes that Clover is a human and has Ed grab them, wanting to add them to the team. Because Martlet lacks anything indicating she is of the Royal Guard, the Five don't believe her status and have her locked away.

Later on, North Star has the Feisty Four, plus other citizens of the Wild East, tied to train tracks as part of Clover's last mission, with Moray, Mooch, and Ace on one side and Edward on the other, much to their discomfort. After the "test" North Star promotes Clover to deputy, much to the indignation of the Four. When Star leaves to get Clover a new badge, the Four gang up on Clover and attack to give them a real challenge. When Star comes back and reprimands them for this, they state their complaints for the unfair attention Star has given to Clover, with Ed calling North Star by his real name; Starlo. When Starlo accuses them of being envious, the Four resign in protest.

Following the fight against Starlo, as Clover and Ceroba travel the Steamworks, the five would later patch things up and become a team again. When Starlo and his posse were preparing a "Welcome Home" party for Kanako, Ed would discover incriminating tapes of Chujin needing a pure human SOUL for experiments, exposing Ceroba's plot. Starlo would chase after her while Ed took Clover back to the Wild East. Moray would call Martlet, who would take Clover to the Ketsukane Estate to investigate. After confirming the truth from the tapes, Martlet convinces the Four not to follow them and Clover when confronting Ceroba, with the Four wishing them good luck and hoping they can play more later.

During the credits, the Four are seen delivering corn from Starlo's parents' farm to the Wild East.

Genocide Route

The Feisty Four are completely absent from the Genocide Route as they are evacuated by the time Clover arrives in town.

Attacks

Ed repeatedly slams his arm down on the bullet board, causing 3 medium-sized boulders to fly into the bullet box.
Two of Ed's hands will appear in the bullet box. If either hand grabs the SOUL, it will return to the center before slamming it on the ground, damaging it.
Moray traps the SOUL in between two swords vertically while two balls bounce around the bullet box.
Moray will swing their sword, which moves up and down quickly. It will switch between being blue and orange.
Ace draws several cards. The cards' locations will flash red three times before moving there. The SOUL must be moved to the empty space.
Ace will draw three cards with suits that will target the SOUL's location.
Mooch spawns three coins at a corner of the bullet box, before a bag appears. Quickly follow the bag because a coin will spawn at the SOUL's location.
Mooch spawns rows of coins that will appear at the top of the bullet box and descend downwards.
Ed and Moray combine their attacks. Moray traps the soul between two swords horizontally while Ed's hand attempts to grab the SOUL.
Ace and Mooch combine their attacks. Ace spawns two cards with four that will target the SOUL while Mooch spawns rows of coins that descend.
Strategy

The battle will switch between Ed --> Moray --> Ace --> Mooch twice, before switching to Ed and Moray, Ace and Mooch, then finally Ed solo for a third time.

Clover needs to survive the battle until Ed attempts his third solo turn (fourth overall), at which point North Star will intervene.

Time to get feisty! [Encounter]
The dream team! [Check, Any]
Smells like teamwork. [Neutral]

Moray leans on Ed to rest up. [Neutral]

Ace is practicing sleight of hand. [Neutral]

You hold your ground while the chaos unfolds around you. [Steady]

You point at the Hospital frantically. They don't notice. [Distract]
You throw sand into the air. Your clothes are dirty. [Distract]
You smirk at the four's antics. They're trying. [Smirk]
Quotes

So ye're the new deputy, eh? Then you shouldn't have a problem dodgin' THIS! [First turn, Ed]
Hello, Clover! I'm very sorry about this, but I've been bored all day! [Second turn, Moray]
Hmph. Good luck. [Third turn, Ace]
Quit hogging Clover! It's my time to shine! [Fourth turn, Mooch]
That's for the train insults, Mooch! Let's see if ya can pass round two, kid! [Fifth turn, Ed]
Nice attack, Edward! You're doing a good job as well, Clover! Ready for this? [Sixth turn, Moray]
Now, now. Quit holding back, everyone. Use your trump cards! [Seventh turn, Ace]
My turn, my turn! [Eighth turn, Mooch]
Moray, let's team up for an attack! [Ninth turn, Ed]
Aww, I would be honored! [Ninth turn, Moray]
Sigh... Mooch? [Tenth turn, Ace]
Of course I'll help you, Ace! Don't be so kind next time. [Tenth turn, Mooch]
[Eleventh turn, Ed]
We ain't done yet. Get ready for my strongest atta-
[North Star] Hey!
Aw man...
Trivia
If the player uses cheats to be able to kill the four in time, they only gain 3 EXP and the following cutscene will play as normal.
Doing so will cause the current member's sprite to glitch out and play Dalv's death animation, as seen here.
If the player uses cheats to kill Ace during the rotation, however, they will perpetually gain infinite EXP (and LV by extension) as Mooch attempts to enter the battle, demonstrated in this video.
Talking with Mooch after first arriving at the Wild East will cause you to lose 1 gold, presumably because she steals it.
Along with Martlet (Neutral/Pacifist), Macro Froggit, Flowey and Asgore, the Feisty are some of the few enemies that are impossible to kill in battle.
When Ed smacks Mooch away in his battle transition, she loses 1 HP.
Along with Starlo and Ceroba, Moray is the only enemy who wields a combat weapon (Their sword).
When each member appears in battle, the battle background changes to a different card suit of various colors, or a pattern of alternating suits if two members are present. In order of appearance, Ed is represented by purple clubs, Moray is represented by dark blue diamonds, Ace is represented by gray spades, and Mooch is represented by green hearts.

entries.name: El Bailador.
entries.content:
El Bailador is one of the minibosses of the Dunes, encountered after the end of the East Mines.

Appearance

El Bailador is a muscular, humanoid monster standing at twice Clover's height. He has red skin with yellow triangular markings running across his collarbone. He has white eyes, a blond feathery mohawk, broad shoulders, and well-defined abs. His mouth is triangular in shape, but forms a 'W' shape when smiling.

He wears a costume reminiscent of a luchador (Mexican wrestler), consisting of long yellow gloves, dark red trunks fastened by a gold belt endorning a rhombus-shaped buckle, and gold knee-length leg armor. His long orange cape with yellow trimming has a lining colored in three vertical strips from left to right: blue, green and red, the reverse order of the dancemat he presents the player. His face appears to be covered by an orange luchador mask with orange eyepieces resembling long lashes. This apparent mask does not seem to cover his mouth, as it visibly moves when he speaks.

Personality

El Bailador greatly enjoys dancing and longs to share his passion with others. He despises solitude and quietness, and uses dance to distract himself from the dire situation of being trapped below the surface. He also wants to cheer the other monsters up and bring joy to the Underground.

Beneath his outgoing, flamboyant demeanor, however, lies a more delicate side. He gets very upset if the player does not share his appreciation for dance, In the Genocide route, he becomes socially awkward and apologizes to Clover for being an inconvenience.

Main Story
Pacifist route

After reaching the East Mines, El Bailador will appear and start talking about the importance of dancing and music, which triggers his battle. After surviving all of his attacks, you're able to spare him.

If done so, he will fly away and later be encounterable again in his Disco in the southern part of Hotland.

If El Bailador is killed, Club Danza will be closed, and an NPC in Hotland tells you that El Bailador isn't answering his phone.

If killed, he will later be a part of Flowey's boss fight as a distorted figurine and attack you.

Genocide route

He appears in the same place and will also talk about dancing and music. This time however, every effort of El Bailador's is useless, Clover is uninterested. El Bailador eventually gets sad and apologizes for the inconvenience, which results in Clover killing him and continuing their journey. If all of the monsters are exhausted before the El Bailador encounter then the fight is skipped entirely.

In Battle
Attacks

El Bailador uses a unique form of attacking where the bullet board is split into three lanes that the player can move into and back by holding down the movement keys. Red, green, and blue bars will come down from the top of the left, middle, and right lanes respectively. As the battle progresses, they will start to come down faster and faster. The player needs to press Z when the bars reach an outlined spot right above their area. If the player misses a bar or presses Z at the wrong time, they will take damage.
In the Genocide Route version of his battle, if the encounters weren't already exhausted, Clover can just move around the bars like normal, and they'll fall down after touching the spots.

Strategy

Much like the previous bosses, Clover can spare El Bailador by dodging for twelve turns.

Trivia
El Bailador's name appears to be a portmanteau of "bailar", meaning to dance, and "luchador." "Bailador" is also the colloquial term for dancer in Spanish, directly translating as "someone who dances".[1]
If you kill El Bailador on a Genocide Route but abort the run during the Axis fight, El Bailador will reappear in Hotland as if you had spared him.
El Bailador and Decibat used to live together on the same apartment floor before both were kicked out after fighting over the volume levels.[2]
If you exhaust the kill counter before encountering El Bailador, he won't appear. Similarly, Decibat won't appear if you exhaust the Dark Ruins kill counter before encountering him.
El Bailador's fight is the only instance of the auto-rhythm function serving a practical use.
References

entries.name: Slurpy.
entries.content:
Slurpy is an NPC found in Snowdin directly north of the first magma puzzle. They are part of a line of sidequests which allow Clover to obtain the Silver Scarf.

Appearance

Slurpy is a white-furred rabbit monster wearing winter clothing. Their outfit consists of a blue beanie, a set of red gloves, a winter coat and some pants.

Personality

Main Story
Pacifist/Neutral Route

Slurpy calls for help and tells you that three dogs dared him to lick the pole, and now his tongue is stuck to the pole, so he asks you to bring a hot item to get his tongue unstuck. Once you free him, he thanks you by rewarding you his Silver Scarf before heading back home.

During the True Pacifist ending, his fate if you complete his quest is shown, with him still stuck if not completed, or swimming in the Honeydew Resort's pool if freed.

Genocide Route

Slurpy is unable to evacuate alongside the rest of Snowdin due to being stuck to the pole. Clover is also unable to assist Slurpy due to the necessary items being impossible to obtain, so they remain stuck to the pole throughout the events of the game.

Sidequest Walkthrough
Upon being greeted initially, Slurpy will ask Clover for some coffee to help thaw their tongue. Upon returning later and attempting to use the Honeydew Coffee, Slurpy will reject it as he deems the coffee too hot.

In order to acquire colder coffee, Clover needs to trade items with the following NPCs:

Trade the Honeydew Coffee with the Lazy NPC (found to the right of Hondeydew Resort) for the Soggy Mitten
Trade the Soggy Mitten with the Mitten NPC (found at the entrance of the Hot Springs) for the Snowdin Map
Trade the Snowdin Map with the Lost Couple (found in front of the the intimidating boulder north of Snowdin's first savepoint) for the Matches
Go back to the Lazy NPC and trade the Matches for the Lukewarm Coffee
Finally, go back to Slurpy and use the Lukewarm Coffee to receive the Silver Scarf

Profile
Appearance

The Honeydew Shopkeeper resembles a pinkish bear. She wears an olive green coat resembling a baker's uniform.

Personality

The Honeydew Shopkeeper is a bubbly service employee, albeit new to Honeydew Lodge as evidenced by her forgetting her lines. She also seems stressed out at times, such as when the player first talks to her, brings up the Honeydew Resort, or seemingly forgetting which grandfather created the resort. The latter of which causes the shopkeeper to bury her head in her arms.

She seems to have found Dalv intriguing, mentioning in her conversation about him that she wanted to talk to him, but the thought of socializing was stressful, before he returned back to the Dark Ruins.

Main Story
Neutral Route

The Honeydew Shopkeeper can be encountered behind the bar in the Honeydew Lodge.

Pacifist Route

Genocide Route

entries.name: Mail whale.
entries.content:
Mail whale is a recurring character in Undertale Yellow. They are assigned a task of delivering mail throughout the Underground and shipping others from one location to another.

Appearance

Mail Whale is a monster resembling a pink whale with a white underbelly and small wings. It wears a blue mailman cap on its head and a bag on its flipper.

Personality

Main Story
Post
A UGPS station
When Clover interacts with a UGPS station, Mail Whale descends from above and gives them mail (provided they have any to offer). Later on in the game, in the farm section of the Dunes, Mail Whale will reveal that Clover can also interact with UGPS stations for Fast Travel, to quickly access previously visited locations that have UGPS stations.

Neutral Route

Mail Whale appears in the Steamworks with a letter from Martlet, giving it to Clover immediately without ring as she had paid premium fee for priority mail. If Ceroba was previously following Clover or a Genocide Route is aborted in the Steamworks, Mail Whale instead appears right outside The Furnace.

Genocide Route

While Mail Whale greets Clover in their initial encounter, they stop appearing altogether once the Snowdin kill count is exhausted.

Trivia
Mail Whale rhymes whenever encountered at a UGPS station. At the Wild East Saloon, it is revealed to be company policy.
If you abort the Genocide Route by not killing all the robots in the Steamworks before fighting Axis, the Mail Whale will appear to give you Martlet's letter in The Furnace, but the UGPS station will still not be useable to pick up new mail or to use Fast Travel.
Mail Whale was first (briefly) shown in the Snowdin trailer, and was officially revealed in the May 2018 Devlog, on Gamejolt.[1]
References
 You’ll be able to receive your mail at a designated UGPS station, scattered around the Underground. A lovely character by the name of Mail Whale will swoop down and deliver the goods whenever the bell is rung. - Game Jolt

entries.name: Mo.
entries.content:
Mo is a raccoon-looking salesman from Snowdin. He can be seen in Snowdin, Dunes and Steamworks, selling you items every time you spot him.

Mo sells these items on his Snowdin stand for 15 G each:

Hot Pop
Lukewarm Pop
Cold Pop
On his Dunes stand, he sells the following items for 20 G each:

Ice Tea
Green Tea
Sea Tea
In Steamworks his stand burns down, but yet he sells you items at 30 G each:

Moss Salad
Flower Stew
Grassy Fries
Profile
Appearance

Mo is dressed in a professional blue suit, complemented by a tasteful pink tie. He completes his outfit with a matching fedora, which features a band in a slightly darker shade of blue, coordinated with his suit. Additionally, he accessorizes with a pair of sunglasses that obscure his eyes.

Personality

Mo is highly motivated by financial success and possesses strong persuasion skills. Furthermore, he maintains a polished yet direct approach in his interactions.

Main Story
Neutral Route

Mo can be encountered during his off-time at the saloon in Wild East. His dialogue there suggest he might possibly be in debt.

Pacifist Route

Upon buying all 3 of Mo's items in all 3 of his stores, Mo will thank you for supporting him, and reveals he has had financial problems recently, and possibly being in debt. But thanks to the player, he might be able to pay off everything.

Genocide Route

Mo passes off Clover's actions as allegations when he encounters them in the Dunes, and sells them stuff like normal.
When Mo reappears in the Steamworks, Clover threatens him and can either rob him of 450G or refrain from doing anything to him.

Trivia
Mo admits to committing theft and tax fraud on the Genocide Route.
In the Genocide Route, his theme music slows once you enter his stand for the 2nd time.
His quote "My deals nut" might be a reference to the word "NUTDEALER" (an anagram of the word UNDERTALE, like DELTARUNE), which is an inside joke of the Deltarune community.

entries.name: Trihecta.
entries.content:
Trihecta are an enemy encountered in Snowdin. It consists of three monsters: Tri, Hec and Ta.

Appearance

Trihecta are 3 ball-shaped monsters who have different colors between them. Tri being the green one, Hec being the red one, and Ta being the blue one. They stack on top of each other from top to bottom.

Personality

Each member of the Trihecta appears to have their own personality. Tri seems to care about their siblings, as evidenced by one of their dialogues when separate. Hec is shown to have low self esteem, and wishes for attention. Ta is shown to be proud, boisterous, and possibly athletic.

Attacks

Circle Bounce: Three spheres bounce on the ground, with one lagging behind the other two.
Circle Reflect: Two large spheres bounce off of either side of the Bullet Box, and when bouncing off one of the spheres moves to another place.
Circle Stack: Three small spheres bounce off the sides of the Bullet Box to a different direction.
Strategy

In order to win against Trihecta, you must push or pull them. Doing either (not both) will make them topple over, allowing you to spare them or to kill them each individually, giving special dialogue on each of their deaths.

entries.name: Frostermit.

entries.name: The Shufflers.
entries.content:
The Shufflers are a group of minor characters who are encountered in Snowdin.

Profile
Appearance

The Shufflers are first introduced in Snowdin where they challenge Clover to a game where they guess which one of the cups has the ball. If Clover wins three times in a row, they can proceed forward

Personality

Main Story
The Shufflers block the path to the Honeydew Resort. In order to get past them, Clover is told to participate in a mini-game where one of them will be hiding a ball and they will shuffle around. Clover has to correctly guess which Shuffler is hiding the ball 3 times to be able to move on. It is also possible to move on by failing at the mini-game too many times. 
They can later be found at the saloon in the Wild East.

Trivia
Each of the three are named after cup-related terms:
Rephil is a combination of "refill" and the given name "Phil."
Swig is a verb for taking a drink from a glass.
Toast is the action of clinking two glasses together.
If the game's fun value is set to 1, Swig will be named Dave.

entries.name: Decibat.
entries.content:
Decibat is a monster that resides in the Dark Ruins, and serves as the game's first mini-boss. This mirrors Undertale proper's Napstablook, who is also the first mini-boss you encounter.

Appearance

Decibat is a bat-like monster with a bluish-gray hue and four wings. The upper pair is notably large and situated where one would expect arms to be, while the lower pair is smaller and closer to the hips. Both sets of wings feature membranes in a light shade reminiscent of dark blue.

He has two large ears whose interiors are adorned with a dark navy blue tone. Markings on his stomach create the illusion of an open mouth, and he has dark blue fluff around his neck. His eyes are completely white with no discernible pupils and he has a large mouth with visible fangs.

Personality

Whhispers only please. Hushh Hushh!

Decibat

Decibat seems like an introverted and sensitive monster who values peace and quiet above all else. He becomes agitated and loses patience when confronted with loud noises. Despite his irritation, he tries to maintain a mostly calm demeanor and prefers to communicate in hushed tones. When speaking, he has an habit of rolling his Hs.

In Battle
Attacks

Wave Blue: Decibat's first attack is a blue wave which can be avoided by not moving.
Wave Orange: Decibat's second attack is an orange wave which can be avoided by moving. At this point, the player is introduced to the concept of blue and orange attacks in Undertale Yellow (if not previously familiar with it from Undertale).
Wave Multi: Decibat sends large sound waves, which are either orange or blue, from all sides of the board except from the bottom, one at a time.
Wave Mini: Small sound waves bounce around the board and change colors from orange to blue or vice versa each time they hit a border.
Stalagmite:[1] Small stalactites appear in a sequence at the top of the bullet board, then fall in the same order.
Strategy

Decibat can be spared by either using the Watch ACT 5 times consecutively or annoying him by using Talk and Shoo ACTs 5 times until he leaves.

entries.name: Micro Froggit.
entries.content:
Micro Froggit is a secret enemy that can be encountered behind the rocks in the room where the Feather can be found.

Appearance

Its appearance is virtually the same as that of its namesake monster. However, its severely diminished size causes it to appear as a single pixel, hence the name Micro Froggit.

Personality

Despite its extraordinarily small size, Micro Froggit is a cheerful monster in spite of its extraordinarily low stats and high risks of being stomped. However, it takes offense when a bigger being waves at it while looking at the wrong direction.

Main Story
Neutral Route

In the dark cavern room, there is a path blocked by large piles of dirt and rocks. Throughout the Dark Ruins, there are many cracks in the walls in the shape of numbers 1 through 5, starting from Dalv's house all the way to the beginning of the Dark Ruins in ascending order (1 to 5). A croak sound is heard when interacting with a crack in the correct order. Though no flavor text is displayed from them when interacting, if Clover interacts with all 5 in ascending order, the dirt-rock barrier in the aforementioned cave is removed, with the narration stating "an ominous presence fills the Ruins," and a small croak sound is heard, presumably Micro Froggit's.

When entering the new room, a Micro Froggit ambushes Clover. If it is spared, another Micro Froggit encounters the first and the two interact before bidding Clover goodbye. Within that room, there is a Golden Pear and a monster hiding from Dalv. You can still encounter Micro Froggit even if you are on a Genocide route.

They can be also found in the secret spa behind the Honeydew Resort (with the Golden Coffee), in the secret cave in the Dunes sandstorm room (with the Golden Cactus), and in the saloon as NPCs. One also appears in a fake battle in the Steamworks immediately preceding the Macro Froggit battle.

Attacks

A comically oversized fly appears in the middle of the Bullet Board and chases Clover's SOUL through the bullet board, similar to one of Sweet Corn's attacks.
Several Micro Froggits jump at the SOUL from the bottom two corners of the Bullet Board.
Strategy

Micro Froggit can be spared by complimenting twice.
Micro Froggit can be killed with a near perfect bulls-eye shot. It can also be killed by ACTing with Stomp.
Flavor Text

Quotes

Trivia
Micro-Froggit is a reference to the ant-sized Froggit found in the room with the three Froggits in Undertale's Ruins.
Their attacks directly parody Froggit's attacks from Undertale. Instead of small flies, Micro Froggit uses one big fly and instead of one big frog they use multiple tiny frogs.
Micro-Froggit uses a special spare animation where the battle box turns yellow that is usually only used for bosses and minibosses; however, this detail is used as an inside joke, and cannot change a genocide run to a neutral without sparing Dalv.

entries.name: Penilla.
entries.content:
Penilla is one of the monsters encountered in the Dark Ruins, and was first revealed in the FIGHT demonstration video.[1] Penilla was conceptualized and drawn by Noteblock, a composer for Undertale Yellow.

Appearance

Penilla is a small monster with a physical appearance similar to a young dinosaur. She also has a few characteristics similar to a pencil, such as the pencil tip at the back of its head and the eraser at the end of its tail. Penilla is also seen carrying a large pencil, which she attacks with.

Personality

Penilla is an artist who does not get along much with the other monsters besides Sweet Corn. She spends a lot of time on her work, supposing that she needs a break.

In Battle

Axis Model 014, better known as Axis, is the boss of the Steamworks, encountered in The Furnace. He is the final model of a line of robots invented by Chujin Ketsukane to serve as mechanical royal guards.

Appearance
Axis is a gray, metallic robot with a large box-shaped head, a round torso, and a single leg with a wheel on the bottom. His head has two pink, unevenly sized eyes and a horizontal line of four bolts or holes resembling a mouth on the front, a vertical antenna ending with a round lightbulb on each side, and a lightbulb and a curled exhaust pipe on the top. His torso has a black heart symbol on the front with four bolts or holes surrounding it, another four bolts or holes in the same arrangement on the back, a light peach-colored gear sticking out the right side, and an exhaust pipe sticking out sideways from each shoulder. His hands wear light peach-colored gloves hover independently of his body, though his shoulder pipes emit smoke clouds that float into his wrists, implying a connection.
Personality
Axis is very persistent when it comes to guarding the Steamworks. Once he catches sight of an intruder, he becomes single-minded in his pursuit of them. Despite his physical agility, his effectiveness as a guardian is greatly hampered by his gullibility and slow wit. He inadvertently allows Clover and Ceroba to escape his capture several times, and easily falls for obvious tricks.
Though he may seem an unsophisticated robot, Axis is a sentient being shown to experience intense, complex emotions. He is short-tempered, easily flustered, and evidently quite foul-mouthed (though his swearing is replaced with milder language by what appears to be a profanity filter). He is also capable of experiencing love; when presented with a 'companion robot' Clover and Ceroba built to distract him with, he becomes besotted with it and declares it his spouse. He also greatly misses Chujin, for his late creator was kind to him. In the Genocide Route, Axis expresses remorse over killing the previous fallen human.
Main Story
Pre-Yellow
Axis went through many failed prototypes, created by Chujin, and was built to serve as a defense mechanism against humans. When showing the eighth and final version to Asgore, it malfunctioned. Sparks flew from the machine, causing a patch of the king's flower bed to set ablaze. Though the fire was quickly put out, Asgore had seen enough; he thanked Chujin for his service to monsterkind and relieved him of his position. Some time later, a human bearing the blue SOUL arrived in the Underground. The human attacked the friend of Chujin's daughter before fleeing to Waterfall. Chujin felt it to be his responsibility to order Axis to hunt down this human, prioritizing giving this order over comforting his daughter. Axis was swift to get the job done, immediately making his way to Waterfall and ending the life of the human. This is later indicated, within the Genocide Route, to be something that Axis did not willingly carry out. Chujin, after all was said and done, was ashamed of the way he'd handled the situation - nevertheless he saw an opportunity. Axis was presumably returned to the Steamworks while Chujin confiscated the human SOUL for experimentation.
Neutral Route
Clover first encounters Axis in the second building of the Steamworks. Axis comes out of a door and notes their various crimes, notably being a human. If Clover tries to plead not guilty, he goes with his nonexistent gut and assumes they are lying. Axis traps Clover in a room that they very easily escape. Axis later follows Clover into the next building and starts a chase sequence, only to crash into a couple of servers.
Pacifist Route
Clover first encounters Axis in the same room as the Neutral Route, though there exists new dialogue as Ceroba will be with the player in Steamworks. Ceroba's presence results in several minor visual changes, such as her incapacitating Axis rather than Flowey at the end of the chase scene, along with changes in dialogue. If Clover interacts with any savepoints, Flowey will not provide additional flavor dialogue with exceptions of when Ceroba is offscreen. The overall gameplay doesn't change drastically though the nullification of one hit is offered by Ceroba at the beginning of each enemy encounter, and the final phase of the Axis Bossfight. If the player chooses to SPARE Axis, the ACT option 'Compliment' is replaced with 'Plan B' in which Clover presents Axis with the 'robot' they created, this will result in Axis having a cutscene of infatuation with the robot. If Clover decides to abort the Pacifist Route through killing Axis, Ceroba will lash out at Clover and exclaim that 'I never want to see you again'. This kill results in special dialogue from Flowey, detailing how Ceroba was only using them anyway. It is revealed in the Ceroba Ketsukane Final Bossfight at the end of Pacifist that she only left Clover due to their soul no longer being “pure”.
Genocide Route
During the Genocide Route, a majority of Clover and Axis' roles are reversed, resulting in Axis being the victim of Clover's murderous rampage. Clover first encounters Axis in the same room as the previously mentioned routes, though the cutscene is essentially inverted. Axis attempts to kill Clover as usual which results in him being shot several times. Axis states his need to 'evacuate' and he escapes through the trapdoor that Clover is normally sent down. During the chase scene, Axis attempts to escape while Clover pursues. Some major encounters are completely skipped, such as Guardener being told to remain down. Once Clover initiates the battle with Axis, he 'draws a weapon' and grabs the trashcan lid that he gives the player on other routes. Axis is impervious to Clover's attacks though once he admits to 'neutralizing' a human, Clover rapidly gains LOVE to 19 and gains the ability to shoot. After being hit by their laser, Axis is split in half through his core, rendering him dead. If Clover aborts the Genocide Route by sparing Axis, he will inform Clover on how much he hates them.
In Battle

* 		Neutral
* 		Genocide

Attacks

During Axis's battle, he will equip Clover with a trashcan lid so they count as a threat. Clover needs to use this lid as a shield to block his attacks.  A lot of Axis's attacks consist of throwing objects from the top of the board. If they hit the ground, Clover will take damage, sharing some mild similarity with El Bailadors attacks. His attacks are:
    * A single ball of energy that comes in a straight line and is used solely and exclusively in the first turn.
    * Energy balls zigzag around the Bullet Board, forcing the SOUL to move from left to right to defend itself.
    * After the first battery loss, Axis' hand grabs the SOUL and places it in the center of the Bullet Board, forcing the player to defend himself from energy balls that come from random directions. If all were defended, it will be the last attack used before Axis charges his red return attack.
    * Axis's hands shot a laser that shoots towards the SOUL in a clockwise direction, before changing direction, after a red exclamation mark beeps.
    * After the second battery loss, a blue line moves across the Bullet Board from left to right as energy balls fall in a straight line.
    * In the middle of Bullet Board, the SOUL needs to defend itself from energy balls while a orange line moves horizontally.
    * While the SOUL is in the deep of Bullet Board, steam attacks rise, with vacant areas ranging between left, middle and right. Happens after the third battery loss.
    * Bombs fall from right and from left, exploding after the SOUL defend itself from them.
    * After the fourth battery loss, Axis summons two generators, leaving him immune to physical attacks. His first attack is to launch energy balls from above while a cross-shaped energy line rotates counterclockwise, having blue and orange in straight line crossing each other.
    * The bombs rotate in different directions to hit the SOUL, which is in the center.
    * After the first generator is destroyed, six balls of energy surround the SOUL and advance towards it, one at a time. The one that will move forward always flashes red.
    * Triggers shoot the SOUL with multiple bullets, coming from random directions. Their location is previously announced by glows, but when they appear, they advance in random directions.
    * The same attack comes after destroying the second generator, but in greater proportion.
    * Balls of energy emerge from random directions to hit the SOUL in the center. Multiple blue lines pass through the Bullet Board in this attack.
    * When hit again, Axis surrounds the protagonist with several balls of energy that advance slowly, making defense easier.
    * The last attack before Axis's last returnable attack: Trigger surrounds the SOUL, and one of them shoots multiples bullets. The one that will shoot will always vibrate beforehand.
Strategy
Clover can fill the Tick-O-Meter at the top right of the screen by blocking attacks. When it is full, Axis will fire a bigger red sphere. Clover needs to deflect this sphere at Axis to deplete his battery depicted as a green meter at the top left of the screen. Alternatively Clover may ATTACK Axis directly while the bar is full for the same effect (should you fail at deflecting the energy ball back at Axis). This obviously has no effect on the pacifist status of the run, but unlike the reflection, Attaching deals damage and can proc ammo like the coffee bean and the glass shards. Once Axis is shut down, Clover can spare him by Complimenting him on the Neutral Route or Plan B on the Pacifist Route. For all of Axis' attacks involving orange lasers, they can be ignored entirely so long as the player is holding the up arrow key, which will keep the soul still while still being registered as moving. To quickly charge the Tick-O-Meter, you should protect yourself from energy balls with the edge of the trash can lid (Energy balls will move towards you faster).

Appearance
Axis is a gray, metallic robot with a large box-shaped head, a round torso, and a single leg with a wheel on the bottom. His head has two pink, unevenly sized eyes and a horizontal line of four bolts or holes resembling a mouth on the front, a vertical antenna ending with a round lightbulb on each side, and a lightbulb and a curled exhaust pipe on the top. His torso has a black heart symbol on the front with four bolts or holes surrounding it, another four bolts or holes in the same arrangement on the back, a light peach-colored gear sticking out the right side, and an exhaust pipe sticking out sideways from each shoulder. His hands wear light peach-colored gloves hover independently of his body, though his shoulder pipes emit smoke clouds that float into his wrists, implying a connection.
Personality
Axis is very persistent when it comes to guarding the Steamworks. Once he catches sight of an intruder, he becomes single-minded in his pursuit of them. Despite his physical agility, his effectiveness as a guardian is greatly hampered by his gullibility and slow wit. He inadvertently allows Clover and Ceroba to escape his capture several times, and easily falls for obvious tricks.
Though he may seem an unsophisticated robot, Axis is a sentient being shown to experience intense, complex emotions. He is short-tempered, easily flustered, and evidently quite foul-mouthed (though his swearing is replaced with milder language by what appears to be a profanity filter). He is also capable of experiencing love; when presented with a 'companion robot' Clover and Ceroba built to distract him with, he becomes besotted with it and declares it his spouse. He also greatly misses Chujin, for his late creator was kind to him. In the Genocide Route, Axis expresses remorse over killing the previous fallen human.
Main Story
Pre-Yellow
Axis went through many failed prototypes, created by Chujin, and was built to serve as a defense mechanism against humans. When showing the eighth and final version to Asgore, it malfunctioned. Sparks flew from the machine, causing a patch of the king's flower bed to set ablaze. Though the fire was quickly put out, Asgore had seen enough; he thanked Chujin for his service to monsterkind and relieved him of his position. Some time later, a human bearing the blue SOUL arrived in the Underground. The human attacked the friend of Chujin's daughter before fleeing to Waterfall. Chujin felt it to be his responsibility to order Axis to hunt down this human, prioritizing giving this order over comforting his daughter. Axis was swift to get the job done, immediately making his way to Waterfall and ending the life of the human. This is later indicated, within the Genocide Route, to be something that Axis did not willingly carry out. Chujin, after all was said and done, was ashamed of the way he'd handled the situation - nevertheless he saw an opportunity. Axis was presumably returned to the Steamworks while Chujin confiscated the human SOUL for experimentation.
Neutral Route
Clover first encounters Axis in the second building of the Steamworks. Axis comes out of a door and notes their various crimes, notably being a human. If Clover tries to plead not guilty, he goes with his nonexistent gut and assumes they are lying. Axis traps Clover in a room that they very easily escape. Axis later follows Clover into the next building and starts a chase sequence, only to crash into a couple of servers.
Pacifist Route
Clover first encounters Axis in the same room as the Neutral Route, though there exists new dialogue as Ceroba will be with the player in Steamworks. Ceroba's presence results in several minor visual changes, such as her incapacitating Axis rather than Flowey at the end of the chase scene, along with changes in dialogue. If Clover interacts with any savepoints, Flowey will not provide additional flavor dialogue with exceptions of when Ceroba is offscreen. The overall gameplay doesn't change drastically though the nullification of one hit is offered by Ceroba at the beginning of each enemy encounter, and the final phase of the Axis Bossfight. If the player chooses to SPARE Axis, the ACT option 'Compliment' is replaced with 'Plan B' in which Clover presents Axis with the 'robot' they created, this will result in Axis having a cutscene of infatuation with the robot. If Clover decides to abort the Pacifist Route through killing Axis, Ceroba will lash out at Clover and exclaim that 'I never want to see you again'. This kill results in special dialogue from Flowey, detailing how Ceroba was only using them anyway. It is revealed in the Ceroba Ketsukane Final Bossfight at the end of Pacifist that she only left Clover due to their soul no longer being “pure”.
Genocide Route
During the Genocide Route, a majority of Clover and Axis' roles are reversed, resulting in Axis being the victim of Clover's murderous rampage. Clover first encounters Axis in the same room as the previously mentioned routes, though the cutscene is essentially inverted. Axis attempts to kill Clover as usual which results in him being shot several times. Axis states his need to 'evacuate' and he escapes through the trapdoor that Clover is normally sent down. During the chase scene, Axis attempts to escape while Clover pursues. Some major encounters are completely skipped, such as Guardener being told to remain down. Once Clover initiates the battle with Axis, he 'draws a weapon' and grabs the trashcan lid that he gives the player on other routes. Axis is impervious to Clover's attacks though once he admits to 'neutralizing' a human, Clover rapidly gains LOVE to 19 and gains the ability to shoot. After being hit by their laser, Axis is split in half through his core, rendering him dead. If Clover aborts the Genocide Route by sparing Axis, he will inform Clover on how much he hates them.
In Battle
